props.name: breaks in activity curves match lattice discontinuities

evidence.quote: It is particularly interesting to note that a break in the activity curves invariably corre- sponds to a point of discontinuity in the lattice dimensions.
the only difference being that the atomic disarrangement occurs within a somewhat wider range of catalyst composition than does the change in preferential catalytic activity.

props.statement: A break in the activity curves invariably corresponds to a point of discontinuity in the lattice dimensions, even for the small zinc oxide percentages that cause the methyl formate peak; the atomic disarrangement occurs within a somewhat wider composition range than the change in preferential catalytic activity.

props.name: catalysis associated with internal crystal structure

evidence.quote: The foregoing re- sults point to an im- portant relation be- tween selective cata- lytic activity and distance between the atoms in mixed cata- lysts.

It is particu- larly noteworthy that catalysis, which apparently is a sur- face effect, seems to be closely associated with the internal structure of the crys- talline catalytic material as disclosed by x-ray analysis.

props.statement: The results point to an important relation between selective catalytic activity and interatomic distance in mixed catalysts; catalysis, apparently a surface effect, seems closely associated with the internal structure of the crystalline catalytic material as disclosed by x-ray analysis.

props.name: copper lattice expands with zinc oxide

evidence.quote: However, the unit-cell sizes of both are markedly influenced by the presence of the other constituent.

the side of the unit cell of the copper lattice expands with increasing additions of zinc oxide, passes through a maximum between 50 and 60 mol per cent zinc oxide, decreases somewhat, and then rises again.
The maxi- mum elongation recorded is 1.3 per cent, corresponding to 90 mol per cent zinc oxide, which is the highest concentration studied.

props.statement: The unit cell of the copper lattice expands with increasing zinc oxide, passes through a maximum between 50 and 60 mol per cent zinc oxide, decreases somewhat and rises again; the maximum elongation recorded is 1.3 per cent at 90 mol per cent zinc oxide, the highest concentration studied.

props.name: catalysts decidedly crystalline at every composition

evidence.quote: The study of the complete series of copper-zinc oxide mix- tures demonstrates that at every composition the catalyst is decidedly crystalline, possessing the characteristic crystal structure of the two components.
The copper has the same structure as that of the metal in bulk, and the zinc oxide has the same structure as when prepared by any other method.
Over the whole range the structure of the catalyst mixtures is decidedly crystalline.

props.statement: At every composition the copper-zinc oxide catalyst is decidedly crystalline, possessing the characteristic crystal structures of the two components: copper with the structure of the bulk metal and zinc oxide with its usual structure.

props.name: essential feature is selectivity of decomposition mechanism

evidence.quote: it was pointed out in the first paper of this series2 that the percentage methanol decomposed varied only slightly after a small percentage of zinc oxide had been added to the relatively inactive pure copper.
Thus, the es- sential feature of these catalysts is their selec- tive nature with respect to the mechanism by which the decomposi- tion occurs.

props.note: based on the decomposition results of the first paper of the series (reference 2), cited
props.statement: Since the percentage of methanol decomposed varied only slightly once a small percentage of zinc oxide had been added to pure copper, the essential feature of these catalysts is their selective nature with respect to the mechanism of decomposition.

props.name: no final conclusions without data on other catalysts

evidence.quote: it is not justifiable to draw any final conclusions or make generalizations in the absence of data on other catalysts.

props.statement: While a simple relation may exist between selective catalytic activity and interatomic distance, it is not justifiable to draw final conclusions or generalize in the absence of data on other catalysts.

props.name: formaldehyde/methyl formate at copper end, CO with zinc oxide

evidence.quote: formaldehyde and particu- larly methyl formate pro- duction is characteristic of the copper end of the dia- gram, while carbon mon- oxide formation is closely associated with the zinc oxide.

props.note: drawn from the cited decomposition data of Figure 2
props.statement: From the decomposition data, formaldehyde and particularly methyl formate production is characteristic of the copper end of the diagram, while carbon monoxide formation is closely associated with the zinc oxide.

props.name: pure zinc oxide changed by methanol-vapor treatment

props.statement: Even in the absence of copper, zinc oxide suffers some change during treatment with methanol vapor at 200-220 °C: the treated pure zinc oxide has a somewhat smaller unit cell than usual, 5.213 A. vs. 5.226 A.

props.name: whether reduction goes to elementary zinc undecided

evidence.quote: It is not possible to de- cide, however, whether this reduction proceeds down to elementary zinc, although the indications are that this is the case.

props.statement: It is not possible to decide whether the reduction of zinc oxide proceeds down to elementary zinc, although the indications are that this is the case.

props.name: selective catalytic activity related to atomic spacing

evidence.quote: The similarity in the shape of the curves in Figures 3 and 4 cannot be coincidental.
The general character of the two diagrams is convincing evidence of a relation between the selective catalytic activity and the atomic spacing of the copper-zinc oxide mixtures.
The results point to a definite relation between the specific catalytic effect and the distance between the atoms of the two components,

props.statement: The similarity in shape of the lattice-dimension curves and the methyl formate and carbon monoxide curves (Figures 3 and 4) cannot be coincidental and is convincing evidence of a relation between the selective catalytic activity and the atomic spacing of the copper-zinc oxide mixtures.

props.name: weight loss not absolutely quantitative

evidence.quote: the results thus obtained are not absolutely quantitative since there is always a possibility of the oxide mixtures not being com- pletely dehydrated when the reduction is started.
Further- more, the loss in weight does not tell whether the zinc is reduced to the free metal or merely to a lower stage of oxi- dation.

props.statement: The loss in weight on reduction is not absolutely quantitative, because the oxide mixtures may not have been completely dehydrated when the reduction started, and it does not tell whether the zinc is reduced to the free metal or to a lower stage of oxidation.

props.name: zinc oxide lattice elongates with copper

evidence.quote: The unit cell of the zinc oxide suffers a similar elongation on addition of copper, with the exception that the curve first passes through a minimum value for 10 to 20 mol per cent copper.

props.statement: The unit cell of zinc oxide suffers a similar elongation on addition of copper, except that the curve first passes through a minimum at 10 to 20 mol per cent copper; the axial ratio remains practically constant.

props.name: zinc oxide partly reduced in presence of copper oxide

evidence.quote: Although zinc oxide is usually considered non-reducible at this temperature, it was, nevertheless, found to be partly reduced by the above treatment when present in mixture with copper oxide.
The reduction manifested itself in the present cata- lyst mixtures by a somewhat greater loss in weight than that corresponding to reduction of the copper oxide alone.
Zinc oxide, ordinarily considered a non- reducible compound, is undoubtedly partly reduced in the presence of copper oxide.

props.limitations: the loss-in-weight results are not absolutely quantitative, since the oxide mixtures may not have been completely dehydrated when reduction started
props.statement: Zinc oxide, ordinarily considered non-reducible, is partly reduced by the methanol-vapor treatment at about 200-220 °C when present in mixture with copper oxide, as shown by a greater loss in weight than corresponds to reduction of the copper oxide alone.

props.name: exothermic copper oxide reduction supplies energy for zinc oxide reduction

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the re- duction of copper oxide by methanol is exothermic and could furnish the necessary energy for the zinc oxide to be reduced when these two compounds are present in an intimate mix- ture.

props.statement: The reduction of copper oxide by methanol is exothermic and could furnish the energy needed for zinc oxide to be reduced when the two are present in an intimate mixture.

props.name: methyl formate from polymerization of formaldehyde

evidence.quote: From these curves it follows that formaldehyde is the principal product of decomposition with pure copper, but that small amounts of zinc oxide greatly favor production of methyl formate, presumably due to polymerization of initially formed formaldehyde.

props.note: interpretation of the cited decomposition data
props.statement: The methyl formate favored by small amounts of zinc oxide is presumably due to polymerization of initially formed formaldehyde.

props.name: product-molecule size vs surface interatomic distance governs specificity

evidence.quote: It seems very likely that one of the governing factors in determining the specific nature of a catalyst is the rela- tion between the size of the molecules of the possible reaction products and the dis- tance between the atoms on the surface of the catalyst.

This effect may be purely geometrical, or it may be the result of a change in the dis- tribution of the residual forces or valences on the sur- face of the catalyst with changing in- teratomic distances.
it will probably serve the purpose better to present these data simply as evidence of the future possibilities in this field of research.

props.note: the authors decline to attempt a specific explanation and present the data as evidence of future possibilities
props.statement: One of the governing factors in the specific nature of a catalyst is very likely the relation between the size of the molecules of the possible reaction products and the distance between the atoms on the catalyst surface; the effect may be purely geometrical or a change in the distribution of residual forces or valences on the surface with interatomic distance.
